children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to open on a strong note on October 21, tracking GIFT Nifty, which was trading with a gain of 97 points at around 23,028.5 in early trade.

Indian benchmark indices snapped their two-day winning streak and witnessed heavy selling on October 19, amid elevated crude oil prices, weak global cues and selling in private banking stocks following disappointing earnings.
At close, the Sensex was down 876.37 points or 1.17 percent at 73,852.90, and the Nifty was down 257.20 points or 1.11 percent at 22,888.95.
The broader markets also remained under pressure with Nifty midcap and smallcap indices fell 1 percent each.
Biggest Nifty losers were Axis Bank, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Bajaj Finance, Trent, Infosys, while gainers included JSW Steel, Eicher Motors, SBI, L&T and ONGC.
Except PSU Bank (gained 2.2%), all other sectoral indices ended in the red with FMCG index down 1.2%, IT index down 1.3% and Private Bank index shed 1.8 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Up)
GIFT Nifty was trading higher at around 23,028.5 in early trade, indicating a positive start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Up)
Asian shares rose along with US equity-index futures as strong earnings from some of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence boom revived optimism over the tech trade.
The MSCI Asia Pacific Index climbed 0.9%, with two shares rising for every one that fell in the gauge. The Kospi Index
rose 3%, with chip heavyweights SK Hynix Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co. gaining at least 5%.
US Equities (Gain)
The Dow rose 1% ​on Tuesday, outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 while the healthcare sector provided Wall Street's biggest boost and technology was its biggest drag.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, the S&P 500 gained 21.84 points, or 0.28%, to 7,712.57 ​and the Nasdaq Composite lost 6.07 points, or 0.02%, to 26,424.82.
Dollar Index (Up)
The dollar index trade marginally higher against the other major currencies.
US Bond Yield (Gains)
The yield on 10-year Treasury and 2-year Treasury were trading higher 5.12% and at 4.78%, respectively.
Asian Currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies were mixed against the US dollar in early trade, with the Indonesian rupiah and Chinese renminbi leading gains, rising 0.3 percent and 0.099 percent, respectively. The Malaysian ringgit edged up 0.012 percent. Meanwhile, the South Korean won declined 0.013 percent, followed by the Taiwan dollar, which slipped 0.037 percent, and the Japanese yen, which fell 0.051 percent. The Philippine peso weakened 0.105 percent, while the Thai baht was the worst performer among the listed currencies, declining 0.196 percent against the previous close.
Crude (Up)
Oil prices edged higher on Wednesday on Middle East supply concerns, with traders wary of Red Sea shipping risks and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
Brent crude futures rose 85 cents, or 0.78%, to $109.64 per barrel as of 0022 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 76 cents, or 0.78%, to $98.58 per barrel.
Gold (Up)
Gold held a decline as conflicting signals
on efforts to end the Iran war clouded the outlook for inflation
and the Federal Reserve’s path for interest rates.
Bullion was trading at around $4,115 an ounce, after
falling more than 1% since the start of the week. Oil was steady
after easing from a five-month high on Tuesday after a diplomat
said reports that an agreement to end the conflict was close
were inaccurate.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold equities worth around Rs 1,148 crore on October 19, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) remained net buyers, purchasing equities worth approximately Rs 3,200 crore during the session.
